We are seeking a seasoned Staff Engineer to help drive our Resilience Engineering team. This role is critical in ensuring the safety and reliability of our production systems through proactive validation techniques, including production load testing and chaos engineering.
 What you’ll do 
 Leadership & Strategy 
 Define and drive the vision for resilience engineering at Affirm, with a focus on production load testing and chaos engineering as first-class engineering practices.
 Tech lead and mentor a team of engineers building platforms and tooling for safe production experimentation.
 Partner with infrastructure, product, and security leadership to embed resilience validation into the software development lifecycle.
 Establish best practices for safely testing system limits and failure scenarios in production.
 Systems & Operations 
 Own the design and evolution of platforms that enable safe, controlled production load testing and fault injection.
 Ensure strong safeguards are in place, including isolation boundaries, approval workflows, and automated rollback mechanisms to protect real users.
 Build systems that provide end-to-end observability, traceability, and auditability for all resilience experiments.
 Drive reliability improvements by systematically identifying weaknesses through load testing and chaos experiments.
 Establish monitoring, alerting, and incident response practices tailored to proactive resilience validation.
 Collaboration & Enablement 
 Work closely with engineering teams to design and execute production load tests and chaos experiments safely.
 Partner with infrastructure teams to build guardrails around tests and experimentations.
 Enable teams to adopt resilience practices by providing reusable tooling, frameworks, and standardized workflows.
 Identify systemic weaknesses and lead cross-functional efforts to improve reliability and fault tolerance.
 Evangelize a culture of “test failure before failure tests you” across the organization.
 What we look for 
 Proven experience leading engineering teams in backend software development or infrastructure development.
 Hands-on experience with production load testing, chaos engineering, or large-scale system validation (nice to have)
 Strong understanding of failure modes in distributed systems, including latency, partial failure, and cascading outages.
 Experience building or operating systems with strong safety guarantees (isolation, rate limiting, guardrails, auditability).
 Familiarity with cloud-native environments (AWS, Kubernetes) and observability tooling.
 Strong programming background (e.g., Python, Kotlin, Java, or similar).
 Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to balance long-term resilience investments with immediate business needs.

As a Data Scientist on the Mapping team, you will collaborate with our world class team of scientists, engineers, product managers, and designers to grow and improve the quality of recommended routes and accuracy of our travel time estimations. We're looking for a passionate, driven Data Scientist who is excited to dive into our geospatial, behavioural and mobility data, and build a best-in-class mapping product that provides safe, efficient, and seamless navigation for our rideshare drivers.
 Data Science is at the heart of Lyft’s products and decision-making. You will leverage data and rigorous, analytical thinking to shape our mapping products and make business decisions that put our customers first. The Mapping team serves models and systems that determine the most efficient routes, fastest travel estimates and process real-time map data signals to detect traffic, closures and slowdowns. Working with our business and analytics partners, the team owns tools to ensure Lyft offers routes that our users trust. This will involve identifying and scoping opportunities, recommending technical solutions, designing experiments, and measuring the impact of new features. You will help us solve some of the most impactful problems in Mapping, including:
 How do we accurately predict acute and chronic traffic conditions?
 How do we improve the recommendations of our routing algorithms?
 How do we keep our travel estimation promises to our riders and drivers?
 How do we benchmark and measure the success of our services?
 Responsibilities:
 Own the complete lifecycle of algorithmic solutions from problem formulation, data exploration, and feature engineering to deployment, monitoring, and iteration
 Prioritize and lead deep dives into our data to uncover new product and business opportunities
 Partner closely with Engineering to build and scale production-grade ML systems, real-time inference services, batch pipelines, and feature stores
 Design, implement, and analyze different types of experiments, and facilitate and foster data-driven and informed decision making and prioritization
 Drive scientific excellence by introducing modern techniques in ML, optimization, reinforcement learning, or graph-based methods to unlock new product capabilities
 Establish metrics that measure the health of our products, as well as rider and driver experience
 Translate complex business challenges into concrete algorithmic solutions in close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Science teams
 Experience:
 Advanced degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, physics, economics, operations research, neuroscience, or engineering, or relevant work experience
 3+ years hands-on experience in a data science or machine learning role working with production machine learning models and optimization systems
 Passion for solving unstructured and non-standard mathematical problems
 Experience independently driving multi-project algorithmic scopes and navigating technical ambiguity from ideation to delivery
 Experience with machine learning models in production, making practical tradeoffs among algorithm sophistication, compute complexity, maintainability, and extensibility in production environments
 Strong oral and written communication skills, and ability to collaborate with and influence cross-functional partners 
 Working knowledge of modern machine learning frameworks and distributed computing systems, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Ray, Spark, etc.
 Benefits: 
 Mental health benefits
 Family building benefits
 Child care and pet benefits
 Subsidized commuter benefits and Lyft ride credits

In this role, you will support and oversee quality and compliance across clinical studies, with a particular focus on imaging-related activities and the CRO vendors contracted to provide imaging services. You will partner with study teams to promote first-time quality, manage quality issues, assess compliance risks and maintain an inspection-ready environment.
Working closely with internal stakeholders, sponsors and external vendors, you will provide technical compliance guidance, support clinical study delivery and contribute to continuous improvement across the Quality & Compliance function.
Key Responsibilities
Facilitate the identification, investigation and resolution of quality issues, including root cause analysis and the development, implementation and monitoring of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans.
Partner with study teams to identify, assess and manage clinical research compliance risks, including protocol deviations and privacy incidents, ensuring timely resolution and escalation where required.
Apply risk-based quality management principles to identify potential compliance issues, assess their impact and support appropriate mitigation strategies.
Monitor quality metrics and key performance indicators, identifying trends and reporting findings to senior Quality & Compliance leadership.
Perform site audits and support study audits and inspections, including preparation, documentation review, coordination and follow-up on findings.
Act as a point of contact between study teams and auditors or inspectors during assigned audits and inspections, supporting preparation, interviews and follow-up activities.
Maintain study inspection readiness by ensuring study documentation is submitted for inclusion in the Trial Master File (TMF).
Oversee study-level training compliance, conducting reviews to ensure assigned training is completed on time.
Provide guidance on ICH-GCP and global quality, regulatory, ethics and privacy requirements, responding to inquiries from study teams, sponsors and customers.
Act as a trusted quality and compliance advisor to internal teams and external CRO vendors, providing practical guidance and technical support, particularly in relation to imaging-related activities.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, identifying opportunities to strengthen quality processes, monitor compliance performance and promote regulatory best practices.

Bachelor's degree (Honours) or equivalent combination of education and experience.
7–9 years of relevant experience in clinical research quality, clinical compliance or clinical risk management.
Demonstrated experience in clinical research and practical application of ICH-GCP principles. Clinical research and GCP experience are essential.
Experience in clinical quality management, compliance risk assessment and risk-based quality management.
Experience supporting or conducting clinical audits, inspections and inspection readiness activities.
Experience in clinical quality issue investigations, protocol deviations, root cause analysis (RCA) and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) management.
Strong knowledge of ICH-GCP principles and global regulations governing clinical research activities.
Knowledge of ISO 20916 and ISO 14155 standards.
Experience in a Project Quality and Risk Lead (PQRL) or similar clinical quality and risk management role within a CRO environment would be advantageous.
Experience in medical imaging, imaging-related clinical research or imaging vendor oversight would be highly advantageous.
Strong analytical, critical-thinking and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify risks, investigate root causes and assess the effectiveness of corrective actions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders, facilitate discussions and provide constructive feedback.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and communicate complex regulatory and compliance requirements effectively.
Knowledge of Quality by Design (QbD) principles.
Fluency in English, with strong written and verbal communication skills.
Industry Experience
Clinical research and clinical trial experience is essential.
Experience within a Contract Research Organisation (CRO) environment is highly desirable.
Experience working with clinical study teams, sponsors and external clinical research vendors is beneficial.
Medical imaging or clinical imaging vendor experience is advantageous.

ABOUT JUNIPER SQUARE

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

As the Senior Compensation & Equity Manager, you’ll own compensation and equity programs end-to-end for a global, distributed workforce, serving as the analytical engine of our Total Rewards function. Reporting to the VP of Total Rewards & People Operations, you’ll partner with Finance, FP&A, Talent Acquisition, and People Business Partners to keep our pay programs market-competitive, internally equitable, and built to scale. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone with deep compensation and equity experience who can add value from day one — owning market pricing, the annual rewards cycle, bonus programs, and equity strategy while giving recruiters and leaders clear, data-backed recommendations. Our Senior Benefits & People Programs Manager serves as your backup on compensation and equity operations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own market pricing and band builds across levels, job families, and geographies (U.S., Canada, India, UK), maintaining the Jobs Table as the source of truth and keeping systems in sync.

 - Lead the annual band refresh, including cost modeling for level and band changes, and review internal pay relativities, job architecture, leveling, and titling decisions.

 - Serve as the first point of contact for comp band, level, and offer recommendations for recruiters and People Business Partners, backed by compa-ratio and internal equity analysis, and advise leaders on promotions, off-cycle adjustments, relocations, and retention packages.

 - Price executive and hard-to-benchmark roles with external advisors where proprietary data is needed, and partner with RevOps and Finance on quota-carrying compensation plans.

 - Run the annual rewards cycle in Pave end to end, modeling budgets by country and reporting cycle outcomes to People leadership.

 - Own the Company Performance Plan and other bonus programs end to end.

 - Administer one-time, spot, retention, and milestone bonuses, including approval workflows and award letters, and partner with the VP of Total Rewards & People Operations and Finance on bonus plan design, including for acquired teams and international populations.

 - Partner with the VP of Total Rewards & People Operations on equity strategy and model equity budgets and Board proposals.

 - Benchmark equity for new hire, promotion, and executive grants, and advise on equity treatment for international moves, new countries, and acquisitions.

 - Own the quarterly grant cycles submitted for Board approval, reconcile equity data across Shareworks, HiBob, and Pave, and lead employee equity education.

 - Use structured candidate compensation data from Ashby to track where we win and lose on pay and flag when a band needs to be revisited, and support pay equity reviews to keep posted pay ranges current.

 - Identify opportunities to automate high-repetition compensation and equity workflows, partnering with the team to embed AI-powered tooling that reduces manual lift without sacrificing accuracy.
   
   
   

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years of compensation experience, ideally within a SaaS or technology company operating across multiple geographies.

 - Deep expertise in market pricing, job matching, and band construction using compensation survey data; Radford experience is strongly preferred.

 - Hands-on experience with equity strategy and operations, including grant guidelines, Board approval cycles, and equity administration platforms such as Shareworks.

 - Experience administering bonus and variable pay plans and running compensation cycles in a platform such as Pave, with advanced spreadsheet and HRIS data modeling skills.

 - Ability to turn analysis into a clear recommendation for leaders, hold a position with data, and exercise sound judgment with highly confidential data.

 - Exposure to international compensation (Canada, India, UK) or sales compensation design, a CCP/CEP certification, or hands-on experience with AI-powered tools such as Claude, is a plus.

 - Exceptional relationship-building skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with shifting priorities.

COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $126,900 - $158,400 USD and the Canadian base salary range for this role is $110,000 - $138,000 CAD. We are flexible on actual base salaries, which will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable.

 

Benefits include:

 - Life insurance

 - Mental wellness coverage

 - Fertility and growing family support

 - Retirement saving plans

 - Annual professional development stipend

About the Risk & Analytics Team 
 The Risk & Analytics (R&A) team makes crucial decisions that direct Affirm’s business strategy. We partner with Machine Learning, Product, Engineering, Capital Markets, and Commercial teams to grow Affirm responsibly by optimizing approval, conversion, losses, and profitability.
 Operating across the entire customer and merchant lifecycle, we tackle a diverse array of challenges, from optimizing checkout conversion and mitigating fraud risk to building scalable data foundations and enabling international growth. We analyze performance not just to report on it, but to determine where to invest resources for maximum impact through building tools, scalable data infrastructure, and analytical frameworks.
 We improve the analytics experience across Affirm by streamlining workflows and fostering a culture of learning and documentation. By taking ownership of the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision, we turn complex data and systems into clear, actionable signals that ensure Affirm grows efficiently and intelligently.
 One Role, Multiple Teams 
 We are hiring multiple Senior Analyst roles across Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization through this single job posting. Rather than interviewing for one specific team, candidates will go through a shared interview process designed to assess the core skills we look for across R&A.
 If selected, we will work with you to determine the best team match based on your interests, experience, strengths, and current business needs. You will have the opportunity to learn more about our teams and share your preferences as you move through the process.
 Potential team placements include:
 Point of Sale (POS): Optimize merchant and checkout performance to improve conversion, approvals, and unit economics across the purchase funnel.
 Direct to Consumer (DTC) / Card: Drive engagement, repeat usage, and lifecycle health across Affirm's app, web, and card experiences.
 Fraud: Prevent and reduce fraud losses across the customer journey while maintaining a frictionless user experience.
 Core Analytics: Build the quantitative research, performance monitoring, and scalable data foundations that enable fast, economically sound decisions.
 Servicing: Enhance the post-origination customer experience by analyzing repayment behavior, collections strategies, and operational efficiency.
 International Expansion: Build the measurement and decision foundations needed to sustainably launch and scale Affirm in new global markets.
 About the Role 
 As a Senior Analyst in Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization, you will join one of several analytical teams working across the customer and merchant lifecycle. While the specific problems you tackle will depend on your eventual team placement, all Senior Analyst roles share a common foundation: owning complex analytical problems end to end, translating data into business strategy, and influencing decisions across technical and non-technical teams.
 You will operate with autonomy to own the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision. You bring exceptional analytical rigor, deep domain expertise, and the ability to translate complex regulatory, economic, and machine learning insights into actionable business strategies. You thrive in ambiguity, balance growth with resilience, and are comfortable operating at both strategic and execution levels to influence stakeholders across the organization.
 What You Will Do 
 Optimize End-to-End Strategy: Leverage advanced data analytics to independently derive insights, develop, and optimize business, risk, or growth strategies across products and geographies.
 Manage Macro & Market Trends: Monitor portfolio performance and exogenous macroeconomic trends, proactively adjusting analytical and operational strategies to mitigate risk and balance growth.
 Model & Capability Building: Partner deeply with Engineering and Machine Learning teams to design, build, and interpret performance metrics for scalable risk, fraud, or growth models.
 Cross-Functional Leadership: Collaborate closely with Product, Legal, and Compliance teams to interpret evolving regulatory and market requirements, translating them directly into analytical policy and product design recommendations.
 Oversee Frameworks & Launches: Oversee the development and execution of analytical frameworks. Drive cross-functional discussions to ensure new product launches and market entries align with risk appetite, operational capabilities, and local regulations.
 External & Strategic Alignment: Engage with external stakeholders, including merchants, vendors, and partners, to align practices, ensure compliance, and strengthen strategic relationships.
 AI Leverage & Mentorship: Build repeatable AI-assisted workflows that compound across the team's analyses, while mentoring junior analysts on technical craft and domain nuances.
 What We Look For 
 2–5 years of proven experience in an analytically driven role within the consumer lending, credit, or fintech industry, specifically leveraging advanced analytics to develop and optimize business strategies.
 Degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, or a related quantitative field.
 Advanced proficiency in SQL, Python, or other scripting languages.
 Deep expertise in data mining, data visualization, and statistical modeling, with experience applying machine learning techniques to business or risk management problems.
 Proven experience leading cross-functional initiatives that bridge Product, Legal, Compliance, and Engineering to align analytical strategies with business objectives.
 Strong understanding of consumer lending regulations, regional market dynamics, and the broader economic landscape influencing policy and growth.
 Demonstrated ability to translate complex regulatory and economic insights into actionable strategies.
 Exceptional communication skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders across technical and non-technical functions.
 Pay Grade - K 
Equity Grade - 4

Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills. Mistplay est le créateur de la catégorie et le leader dans l'espace de fidélisation mobile « jouer-pour-gagner » (play-and-earn), conçu pour récompenser les joueurs.
LoyaltyPlay est notre plateforme de monétisation B2B, un puissant Centre de Récompenses de Jeu (Gaming Reward Hub) conçu pour les éditeurs d'applications mobiles. Cela crée une boucle d'engagement profonde et un puissant canal de monétisation pour l'éditeur.
Il s'agit d'un rôle à fort impact qui consiste à vendre une solution de monétisation différenciée et axée sur la performance à un public mondial d'applications mobiles.
L'opportunité
Mistplay est à la recherche d'un leader des ventes nord-américain expérimenté pour assurer un leadership concret auprès de notre équipe croissante et distribuée. Il s'agit d'un rôle central de « joueur-entraîneur » (player-coach), conçu pour un leader qui excelle en matière d'excellence opérationnelle, de gestion de la performance et de stratégie de transactions de haut niveau.
Nous ne cherchons pas un dirigeant traditionnel pour siéger derrière un tableau de bord; nous avons besoin d'un praticien qui peut entraîner de manière crédible des vendeurs chevronnés, plonger dans des négociations d'entreprise complexes et insuffler une culture de responsabilisation et d'exécution constante dans toute la région.

Diriger et encadrer: Gérer une équipe distribuée de Directeurs de comptes expérimentés, en leur offrant la priorisation et le soutien quotidiens dont ils ont besoin pour réussir.
Stratégie de transactions: Agir en tant que « parrain exécutif » sur les transactions majeures avec les entreprises, en participant à des réunions de grande valeur pour apporter un poids stratégique et aider à naviguer dans les cycles complexes d'approvisionnement et juridiques.
Rigueur opérationnelle: Travailler en partenariat avec la direction pour concevoir des objectifs réalistes et des plans de commissionnement qui incitent aux bons comportements.
Gestion de la performance: Maintenir une visibilité approfondie sur le pipeline nord-américain, identifier les goulots d'étranglement et fournir un encadrement réfléchi pour aider les représentants à se surpasser.
Collaboration interfonctionnelle: Servir de pont entre les ventes, la réussite client (Customer Success) et les opérations pour garantir que notre « victoire » sur le marché est soutenue par une expérience interne fluide.
Architecture de processus: Créer une structure et une cohérence pour l'ensemble du processus de vente sans ajouter de « bureaucratie pour le plaisir de la bureaucratie ».
Who you are
Leader éprouvé: 10 à 15 ans d'expérience dans la vente interentreprises (B2B), dont une partie importante dédiée à la gestion de représentants de haut niveau et très performants.
Entraîneur crédible: Vous avez été un contributeur individuel de premier plan par le passé et vous pouvez vous affirmer lors d'une transaction de 7 chiffres. Vous dirigez par le respect et l'expertise, et non par la microgestion.
Pragmatique et sans égo: Vous êtes une personne d'action (« doer ») à l'aise dans un rôle vaste et collaboratif. Vous vous souciez plus du succès de l'équipe que du titre ou de la hiérarchie.
Mentalité opérationnelle: Vous possédez un excellent jugement commercial et savez comment élaborer des plans d'incitation et des flux de travail de vente qui fonctionnent réellement sur le terrain.
Habitué au travail à distance (Remote-Fluent): Vous avez de l'expérience dans la direction d'équipes distribuées à travers différents fuseaux horaires et savez comment maintenir la culture et la performance de l'équipe à distance.
Expérience idéale
Expérience dans les partenariats de jeu (Gaming), AdTech, ou SaaS à forte croissance.
Expérience de la gestion des cycles de vente complets (« full-cycle »), y compris l'acquisition de nouveaux comptes et l'expansion des comptes existants.
Capacité éprouvée à travailler efficacement avec des parties prenantes de niveau C dans des organisations de type Fortune 500.

Impact immédiat: L'équipe se sent plus soutenue localement grâce à une orientation quotidienne et une priorisation plus claires.
Vitesse des transactions (Deal Velocity): Les opportunités stratégiques progressent plus rapidement dans l'entonnoir grâce à votre implication directe dans l'architecture des transactions.
Cohérence: La région nord-américaine devient un « moteur prévisible » pour l'entreprise, avec une grande visibilité sur le pipeline et une atteinte des quotas cohérente.

As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you!

 


THE ROLE

In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include:

 - Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.

 - Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).

 - Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!

 - Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.

 - Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.

 - You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.

 - If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!

 


THE QUALIFICATIONS

We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

 - You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.

 - You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.

 - You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.

 - You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team.

 - You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.

 - You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.

 


WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

 


WHY YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY

 - You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.

 - You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.

 - You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).

 - You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

 - To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.

 - You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.

 


ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 


MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 


COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

About 1Password

We're hiring a Senior Manager, Infrastructure Security to lead the team responsible for securing 1Password's cloud-native platform. Reporting into Platform Security, you'll set the direction for Infrastructure Security, establish priorities, and drive execution aligned with our broader security strategy.

We're looking for a hands-on engineering leader who combines deep technical expertise with strong judgment and people leadership. You'll help your team tackle complex security challenges, prioritize work that meaningfully reduces risk, and build strong partnerships with engineering teams to make security an integral part of how our platform evolves.

Your team is responsible for security across cloud infrastructure, identity and access management, privileged access, networks, containers, and emerging AI and automated systems. You'll lead and develop a team of security engineers while partnering closely with Platform Security, Threat Operations, and infrastructure engineering leaders to strengthen our security posture.

As AI and agentic technologies become increasingly integrated into production environments, you'll also help define how we secure these systems, including their identities, access to infrastructure and data, and the controls that limit potential risk.

In this role, you'll help ensure 1Password's infrastructure remains secure, resilient, and scalable while enabling engineering teams to move quickly and confidently.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

We're looking for someone who brings strong technical depth, direct people leadership experience, and the ability to turn a security strategy into shipped work.

 - 8+ years of experience in security engineering, including at least 3 years directly managing a team, with demonstrated accountability for team delivery, individual performance, engagement, and professional growth.

 - Deep production experience securing a major cloud platform, including identity and trust boundaries, workload isolation, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code.

 - Experience building or improving privileged access programs, including how people and workloads access the systems and resources they need.

 - Experience implementing network segmentation, WAF, and zero-trust approaches at scale.

 - Hands-on experience securing AI and agentic systems in production, including workload identities, access to infrastructure and data, and security boundaries designed to limit the impact of a compromised agent.

 - Demonstrated ability to review technical work, identify gaps, and raise the quality of engineering outcomes through effective technical oversight and coaching.

 - Ability to navigate ambiguous, complex problems, establish priorities within an area of ownership, and define technical direction without relying on prescribed solutions.

 - Proven ability to influence engineering teams through technical credibility, a track record of delivering results, and the development of high-performing engineers.

 - Experience using AI to improve individual and team effectiveness, modeling responsible adoption, and ensuring AI-assisted work is reviewed for accuracy, sound judgment, and impact.
   
   

What you can expect:

 - Set the strategic direction and priorities for Infrastructure Security, and own delivery end to end, aligned with the Platform Security strategy

 - Define clear goals and metrics so progress is measurable and trade-offs can be argued with evidence

 - Lead delivery across concurrent workstreams in cloud security, identity and access management, and container security

 - Build, coach, and grow a team of security engineers: set clear expectations for what good looks like, and address both strong performance and off-track performance early rather than waiting for issues to surface

 - Work closely with platform and infrastructure engineering teams so security is designed into systems from the start

 - Help define how we secure AI and automated systems, including the identities they run as, how their access is scoped, and where the boundaries around them sit

 - Partner with the other Platform Security teams and with Threat Operations so findings reach the right owner and get remediated inside an agreed SLA

 - Make the calls Infrastructure Security needs, and bring in your peers and manager on decisions that reach beyond the team

 - Make sure security keeps up with company growth without slowing teams down

 We are building a small, hands-on marketing team with one job: turn conferences and useful content into qualified conversations with the right buyers at brands, retailers and 3PLs. The team runs two motions: 
 Conference and buyer events: we attend a conference because the right buyers are there and a practice has a relevant offer, and we add dinners, roundtables or expert sessions when that improves access to those buyers.

 Interview practice leaders and customers to extract real evidence and original perspective; maintain an approved claims register and never publish a claim that has not been verified and approved. 
 Write thought leadership that demonstrates expertise through specifics, examples and source-backed reasoning.

 Discoverability: SEO, GEO and AEO

 100% of material factual claims supported and approved before publication; every priority asset has an audience, intent, call to action and distribution plan.

 Growth in non-brand search visibility and qualified visits, and inquiries from content that Sales accepts as qualified. AI-answer visibility is tracked as a diagnostic, not a quota.

 Rigorous fact-checking, customer permissions and AI editing. Consistent brand narrative and tone across channels. 
 Reliable ownership of briefs, reviews, deadlines and asset maintenance in a small, fast-moving team.

About Us: 
 At Reusables, we’re driven by a vision of a waste-free world and recognize the urgent need to address the environmental impact of our current systems and habits. We believe that meaningful change requires institutions to offer frictionless systems that make sustainability effortless and tangible. 
 What began as a grassroots initiative offering reusable takeout containers to restaurants and cafes in Vancouver, has since grown into an enterprise technology platform reaching institutions across North America. Today, Reusables is helping to eliminate thousands of tonnes of single-use waste each year, empowering businesses to join the journey toward a cleaner, more sustainable future. 
 As a venture-backed and mission-driven company, we are passionate about making impact at scale. We are a young, weirdly talented group of ‘high-octane’ individuals that are relentlessly focused on the planet, people, and profit – in that order. 
 About the Role: 
 You'll own everything outside our door: getting the right parts to our floor at the right cost and time, and getting finished units across borders and onto campuses. That covers sourcing and procurement from suppliers in North America and Asia, inbound and outbound logistics, customs and tariffs. 
 You'll be our first dedicated supply chain hire, so you’ll get to design the end-to-end supply chain that best fits our products and demand cycles, and watch it become a core part of how Reusables runs. Very little of what we do has been done before, so most of what you set up will be one of a kind. Until our Production Manager starts, you'll also cover inventory planning and make sure the floor has what it needs. This is a full-time, permanent position to start in January 2027. 
 Our hardware is designed, built, tested and shipped by a small team in Vancouver, and you’ll report to our Hardware Lead. Most units ship in a summer peak, ahead of each autumn semester. 
 We’re moving from build-to-order to levelled production. From February we build steadily towards the September peak, and servicing and refurbishing units already in the field runs alongside new builds. 
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Buy components and purchased units, from electronic and mechanical parts to tablets, displays and enclosures, at the right cost and lead time 
 Be the main contact for our suppliers: negotiate price, MOQs and lead times, track delivery performance and resolve quality issues 
 Own supplier, cost, lead time and MOQ for every part, and bring lower-cost or more available substitutes to engineering for approval 
 Find single-source and long-lead parts, and qualify second sources before they become shortages 
 Turn the production plan and sales pipeline into a forecast, and set reorder points 
 Order ahead of factory shutdowns such as Chinese New Year 
 Arrange inbound freight and outbound shipments to customers in Canada and the US: carriers, rates, tracking and delivery dates 
 Handle HTS classification, country of origin, CUSMA documentation, duties and tariff exposure, working with our customs broker 
 Design and source packaging that protects the product and keeps freight costs down 
 Set the packing specs our production floor follows 
 Set up the inventory and BOM data and tools we need as we grow 
 Report on spend, landed cost per unit, supplier on-time delivery and inventory value 
 How Your Year Looks: 
 January to February: Take over the costed BOM and supplier list, and get orders for the build-ahead and summer peak placed before the Chinese New Year shutdown 
 February to May: Keep parts flowing for levelled production, qualify second sources, and cover inventory planning until our Production Manager is in place 
 June to September: Outbound shipping to campuses in Canada and the US, customs clearance, and chasing anything late 
 October to December: Post-season review of landed cost and supplier performance, and next year's forecast and ordering plan 
 What You’ll Bring To The Team: 
 4+ years in procurement or supply chain at a hardware or electronics manufacturer 
 Experience sourcing electronic and mechanical components, including from suppliers in Asia 
 Working knowledge of Canada–US import and export: HTS codes, CUSMA, tariffs and customs brokers 
 Enough technical depth to read a BOM and a drawing and judge whether a substitute part is a real fit 
 Strong spreadsheet skills and experience with an ERP, MRP or inventory system 
 A strong negotiator who follows through on the details 
 Eligible to work in Canada, and able to work on-site in Vancouver 
 A positive, go-getter attitude: you’re excited by a new challenge every day, and you’ll figure out what you don’t know yet 
 Self-motivated and high ownership: give you a problem and you’ll own it through to the end, without waiting to be told how 
 No ego: we’re focused on the mission and check our egos at the door 
 Nice to have 
 Experience building a supply chain function at a startup 
 APICS CPIM or CSCP, or SCMP designation 
 Experience with PCB assembly houses or contract manufacturers 
 Experience planning inventory for seasonal demand 
 If your background doesn’t perfectly align with the qualifications listed, but you’re confident in your ability to excel in this role, we still want to hear from you! At Reusables, we value diverse experiences and unique perspectives, so don’t hesitate to apply if you believe you can make a meaningful impact. We hire for attitude first. Skills can be taught, so we’d rather meet someone who takes on any task with excitement and figures it out, than someone held back by what they’ve done before. 
 We sincerely appreciate the time and effort of all applicants who express interest in joining our team. While we carefully review each application, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you for considering Reusables as your next career opportunity! 
 Compensation & Key Criteria
 Please note: This is an in-office position at our office in Vancouver, BC. 
 Compensation: $90,000-110,000 CAD per year 
 Start date: January 2027 
 Reports to: Hardware Lead 
 Why You’ll Love Working At Reusables: 
 Benefits package (dental, vision, health) 
 Membership to Outdoor Prolink for discounted outdoor gear 
 A small, fun, low-ego team that loves the work we do together and the impact we have 
 A central, spacious and easy-access office in Vancouver with a friendly, sociable atmosphere and plenty of space to focus 
 Annual offsite with the entire Reusables team 
 Work that ships: what you build, buy or plan ends up on campuses where people use it every day 
 Our Values: 
 Strive for excellence 
 Assume you have something to learn from everyone 
 Play bigger 
 Check your ego at the door 
 See the path forward, not the trees in the way 
 Why Join Us: 
 The ocean already contains 165 million tonnes of plastic, and by 2050, plastic waste could outweigh fish. While recycling is often touted as the solution, only 5% of plastic is actually recycled in the U.S. (9% in Canada). Governments and businesses worldwide are banning single-use plastics and committing to zero-waste solutions by 2030. 
 Reusable packaging is the most sustainable alternative, but adoption has been hindered by cost and operational complexity. Reusables removes these barriers, offering a scalable, tech-enabled solution for food businesses and the institutions that serve them.

In 1931, electrical draftsman Harry Beck looked at London’s Underground map and saw a system that had become too complicated to understand.
 The maps at the time tried to represent the city geographically. Beck realized that wasn’t what riders actually needed. What mattered was how the system connected: which lines went where, where you could transfer, and the simplest way to get from one place to another. So he redrew the network around those relationships instead. His design became the foundation for the modern Tube map and changed how people navigated London.
 Mercury’s Customer Experience organization has its own increasingly complex network.
 As Mercury grows, the right place for support work will keep changing. Some new or complex work may benefit from starting in an incubation team before we know how it should scale. From there, it might move into Core Support, remain specialized, transition to an outsourced partner, or become increasingly supported by AI-powered tooling. The challenge is knowing where work belongs at each stage of its lifecycle, when it’s ready to move, and how to make those transitions without compromising the customer experience.
 For the first 9–12 months, a significant majority of your work will focus on our growing BPO partnership. You’ll identify opportunities to expand the work we deliver through that partnership, build the operational and financial case for doing so, align CX leadership around those recommendations, and lead approved transitions from initial scoping through stabilization.
 Over time, the scope will broaden. You’ll apply the same thinking across our wider service delivery ecosystem, helping us evaluate when work should enter an incubation model, when it is ready to graduate, and whether its next home should be Core Support, a specialized team, an outsourced partner, AI-powered tooling, or another model as our capabilities evolve.
 You won’t be the sole decision-maker on where work lives. Your role is to develop the recommendation: bring together the data, customer impact, operational realities, and tradeoffs; build a compelling case; and help CX leadership reach a well-informed decision. Once a direction is approved, you’ll own the program that turns it into reality.
 This is a role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally energized by building a strong argument for how our service delivery model should evolve and by working through the operational details required to make that change succeed.
 In this role, you will: 
 Lead high-impact programs that evolve how CX delivers support, with the first 9–12 months heavily focused on expanding and optimizing our BPO partnership.
 Identify opportunities to move work to a different service delivery model and build the case for change using customer, operational, and financial data. This could include recommending that emerging or complex work move into incubation, as well as determining when incubated work is mature enough to transition into Core Support, a specialized team, or our BPO partnership.
 Help define what makes work ready to move. Develop clear criteria for when a workflow needs incubation, when it has reached sufficient maturity and stability to graduate, and which delivery model is best positioned to own it next.
 Evaluate where AI-powered tooling could take on, augment, or reshape support work, and partner with the right teams to build a clear case for when automation creates a better customer and business outcome.
 Lead approved service delivery transitions end to end, whether work is moving into incubation, graduating from incubation, transitioning between internal teams, or moving to an outsourced partner. Own the program from initial scoping and business case through readiness, migration, ramp, stabilization, and handoff into long-term operations.
 Partner across Workforce Management, Enablement, QA, Support, and other teams to build transition plans that account for capacity, training, knowledge transfer, quality, tooling, and operational readiness.
 Define success before a transition begins and measure whether the change actually delivered the intended customer, quality, capacity, and cost outcomes.
 Establish clear readiness and stabilization criteria so transitions are judged by whether they work, not simply whether they launched on time.
 Bring structure to complex, ambiguous service delivery questions, identifying the right analysis, stakeholders, dependencies, and tradeoffs required to move from uncertainty to a clear recommendation.
 Build repeatable frameworks and approaches that make future service delivery decisions faster, clearer, and more consistent.
 Use what we learn from each transition to continuously improve how Support evaluates where work should live and how changes should be executed.
 We’re looking for someone who: 
 Has 6+ years of experience in strategic program management, customer experience operations, service delivery, outsourcing, support operations, or a related field.
 Has deep experience with outsourced service delivery and has personally led significant transitions of operational work into a BPO or similar partner environment.
 Understands the operational machinery behind successful BPO transitions, including workforce planning, forecasting, training, knowledge transfer, quality management, ramp planning, and stabilization.
 Can build a strong recommendation without needing to own the final decision. You know how to gather the right evidence, frame tradeoffs clearly, anticipate objections, and create alignment among senior stakeholders.
 Thinks in systems. You naturally look beyond the performance of an individual team to understand how the broader service delivery model works and where changing it could produce a better outcome.
 Is analytically rigorous and commercially minded. You’re comfortable working with operational and financial data, testing assumptions, building business cases, and making recommendations when the answer isn’t obvious.
 Exercises strong judgment in ambiguous environments. You can take a question like “Is this still the right place for this work?” and determine what evidence, tradeoffs, and perspectives are needed to answer it well.
 Can move seamlessly from recommendation to execution. You’re as comfortable developing the case for a service delivery change as you are working through the details required to make it successful.
 Influences effectively without relying on formal authority. You know how to align teams with different priorities and constraints around a shared outcome.
 Communicates complex decisions with clarity. You can explain the customer impact, operational implications, economics, and tradeoffs behind a recommendation without burying the decision in the analysis.
 Holds a high bar for outcomes, not just completion. You care whether a transition delivered what we expected and are willing to revisit assumptions when the data tells us otherwise.
 The ideal candidate may also have: 
 Experience designing or evolving a multi-tier customer support service delivery model.
 Experience with BPO expansions, outsourced operations, vendor launches, or team and site stand-ups.
 Experience moving work between different internal delivery models, such as from incubation to Core Support or between specialized and scaled support teams.
 Experience evaluating how automation and AI-assisted support change the economics, complexity, or appropriate placement of customer support work.

 Experience using SQL, Google Sheets, or business intelligence tools to evaluate operational performance and build business cases.
 Experience in fintech, financial services, or another regulated environment where risk and operational complexity influence how work can be delivered.

Job Description: 
 The Manager, DR Strategy & Adequacy provides specialized 2LOD challenge of disaster recovery strategy, recovery architecture, DR testing adequacy, and alignment between technology recovery design and business expectations. The role assesses whether recovery strategies are viable at scale and whether DR capabilities can support critical operations within defined tolerances and RTO/RPO expectations.
 What will you do? 
 DR Strategy & Design Challenge 
 Review and challenge enterprise DR strategy, architecture patterns, recovery design, failover models, active-active/active-passive approaches, and recovery orchestration assumptions.
 Assess whether DR strategies are aligned to critical operation impact tolerances, RTO/RPO requirements, dependency mapping, and business continuity expectations.
 Identify and document gaps between technology recovery design, business tolerances, and demonstrated recoverability.
 Assess recovery dependencies, single points of failure, and concentration risks that could affect recovery of critical operations.
 Review resilience impacts associated with material technology changes, platform migrations, and changes to recovery strategies.
 Testing Adequacy & Evidence Review 
 Challenge the adequacy, risk basis, scope, and realism of DR testing plans, including failover/failback exercises, application recovery testing, end-to-end testing, and testing after onboarding or material change.
 Challenge testing against severe-but-plausible scenarios, including regional, cloud, shared-service, and concurrent technology disruptions.
 Assess whether testing demonstrates end-to-end recovery of critical operations and validates key upstream/downstream recovery dependencies.
 Review and challenge test evidence, exceptions, constraints, remediation actions, and closure documentation to determine whether recovery capability is credibly demonstrated.
 Escalate unsupported recovery assumptions, insufficient test coverage, recurring test limitations and any material gaps through established issue and governance processes.
 Insight, Monitoring & Reporting 
 Contribute to DR-related KRIs, RAS measures, trend reporting, and management insights on recovery strategy maturity and residual risk.
 Support enterprise reporting on DR adequacy, technology recovery gaps, and progress against remediation commitments.
 Provide insights into governance reporting on backup/data resilience posture, trends, root causes, and remediation progress.
 Maintain challenge records, issue linkages, and evidence documentation that is clear, evidence-based, and suitable for audit, regulatory, and management review.
 Identify recurring recovery themes, emerging risks, and dependency concerns requiring leadership and stakeholder attention.
 Stakeholder Partnership 
 Partner with DBTS, Enterprise Architecture, Technology Resilience, Operational Resilience, BCM, Cyber, TPRM, and Business Group stakeholders to promote alignment between technology recovery and business resilience outcomes.
 Provide practical guidance on evidence expectations and remediation adequacy while preserving 2LOD independence.
 Support continuous improvement of DR review playbooks, test challenge criteria, and issue closure standards.
 Support risk-based oversight planning by identifying technologies and recovery capabilities requiring enhanced oversight.
 Expected Outcomes / Measures of Success 
 DR strategies are challenged for feasibility, scalability, and alignment with business impact tolerances.
 DR testing demonstrates credible recovery capability rather than isolated execution evidence.
 Observed material gaps in recovery design or test adequacy are captured, escalated, and tracked to remediation.
 Senior management has clearer visibility into DR adequacy and residual recovery risk.
 What do you need to succeed? 
 Experience with disaster recovery strategy, recovery architecture, failover/failback models, recovery orchestration, application recovery, infrastructure resilience, cloud/hybrid environments, and technology risk oversight.
 Understanding of operational resilience, BCM/DR lifecycle, RTO/RPO, E-21, B-13, KRIs, issue management, and 2LOD challenge practices.
 Ability to review technical evidence, identify unsupported assumptions, and produce concise risk-based conclusions.·   Strong stakeholder engagement, analytical, written communication, and constructive challenge skills.
 University degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
 Typically 7+ years of experience in disaster recovery, technology resilience, technology risk, operational resilience, business continuity, or related fields.
 Professional certifications such as CBCP/MBCI, DRI/BCI, CRISC, CISM, ITIL, cloud resilience, or equivalent are assets.
 What’s in it for you? 
 We’re proud to be recognized as a company with a 2026 Most Trusted Executive team by Great Place to  Work® Canada
 Access to short-term assignments or ‘Gigs’ across the organization, to help you develop new skills and connections.
 A collaborative and interactive team environment
 Charitable giving through our You Give, We Give program lets you give back to your community – and in many  cases, we’ll match your contributions.
 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to  support your well-being.
